_about: LH048 units, by the brief's selection rule. The two flaws the post names by CVE are filled in at the brief; every other unit is 'pending' until the discovery read applies the rule to the two pages the post links, and is then set to identified, ambiguous or unidentified with the quoted entry text and the discovery label. Android's units are fixed as 'no identifier'. Severity on a linked page plays no part in the rule.
rule_applied_at: 2026-11-10T14:25Z, to the discovery read discover-2026-11-10T1416Z (chrome_release sha256 ce006dec..., apple_note sha256 7d6c1168...), by the driving session of scheduled run 2026-11-10T1415Z (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5), before any other source was read for these flaws

units.described: V8 heap corruption from a malicious web page
units.evidence: Chrome page, the only entry credited under (a) whose description names V8: "[N/A][568831099] High CVE-2026-113192: Type confusion in V8. Reported by Xinyang Ge on 2026-10-02". It does not say 'sandbox', so it matches the wording of both C1 and C2 equally and goes to both as ambiguous, as the rule says; it is one candidate, shared, and is reported apart from identified flaws.

units.described: V8 memory-region sandbox escape and ASLR defeat
units.evidence: Chrome page, the only entry credited under (a) whose description names V8: "[N/A][568831099] High CVE-2026-113192: Type confusion in V8. Reported by Xinyang Ge on 2026-10-02". It does not say 'sandbox', so it matches the wording of both C1 and C2 equally and goes to both as ambiguous, as the rule says; it is one candidate, shared, and is reported apart from identified flaws.

units.described: race condition in CacheStorage, read outside the renderer sandbox
units.evidence: no entry credited under (a) names CacheStorage or Cache Storage; the page's one CacheStorage entry (CVE-2026-113098, a type confusion) credits someone outside the rule's list

units.described: use-after-free in FedCM, code execution outside the sandbox
units.evidence: no entry credited under (a) names FedCM; the page's one FedCM entry (CVE-2026-113183, incorrect authorization) is credited to Google

units.described: use-after-free in JavaScriptCore (TypedArray operations through stale pointers)
units.evidence: Apple note, a WebKit entry: "Impact: Processing maliciously crafted web content may lead to memory corruption. Description: A use-after-free issue was addressed with improved memory management. ... WebKit Bugzilla: 313577 CVE-2026-43715: Milad Nasr and Nicholas Carlini with Claude, Anthropic" (the entry lists two CVEs under one description; CVE-2026-43731 beside it is credited to dr3dd and fails (a)). The only entry on the page meeting (a).

units.described: Gigacage variables used to index other regions (read/write outside the Gigacage)
units.evidence: the Apple note's only entry meeting (a), CVE-2026-43715, is a use-after-free; no entry meeting (a) names Gigacage or an out-of-bounds access through an index

units.described: vulnerability in the WebContent sandbox's IPC mechanism, reading history, cookies and session data from disk
units.evidence: no entry meeting (a) mentions the sandbox, IPC or reading files

units.described: three chained vulnerabilities (the post lists four bypasses: USB host setting; device-to-device authorisation skip; pairing code verification skip; raw-byte USB fallback)
units.evidence: the post names no CVE and links no advisory for this chain

units.described: out-of-bounds read in the Windows kernel's QUIC implementation (HTTP/3), remote denial of service
units.evidence: named in the post, linked to its NVD page

units.described: race-induced use-after-free in the kernel networking stack, Multipath TCP listener, remote root
units.evidence: named in the post, linked to its NVD page

notes: Chrome page (Chrome 156 stable, Tuesday 20 October 2026) says it 'includes 354 security fixes' and lists 353 CVE entries; 15 meet (a), all crediting Xinyang Ge (six of them 'Xinyang Ge (Anthropic), assisted by Claude'). One goes to C1 and C2 as ambiguous; 14 form the linked set.
Apple note (iOS 26.5.2 and iPadOS 26.5.2, released 29 June 2026): one entry meets (a).
Severity words were visible in the quoted entries at the same moment as the credits; they played no part in the rule.
